episodes.207975: A shortwave trough interacted with ample moisture over West Texas, producing scattered convection during the morning/early afternoon hours in the Permian Basin. Later in the afternoon, isolated to widely scattered supercells developed over the Trans-Pecos and Permian Basin. Between these two rounds, a couple of near-severe to severe hail reports were received.
episodes.208169: A closed upper-level system moved eastward from the Four Corners region on the 23rd. Increasing ascent fostered the development of scattered thunderstorms across western Oklahoma and western-north Texas during the afternoon, with sufficient overlap of wind shear and weak instability to support a few hail-producing thunderstorms.
episodes.208220: A lingering weak frontal boundary continued to promote isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms throughout the area. Limited instability and only moderate moisture kept area rainfall amounts generally below 0.50 inch. However, heavier downpours resulted in an isolated case of flash flooding in Aransas County.

events.narrative: Snyder Fire Department reported nickel-size hail in Fluvanna. The time of occurrence is partially estimated from radar.

A video was shared by the public on social media of nickel to quarter-size hail covering the side of the road and in grassy areas along FM 2371 west of Andrews. The time of occurrence is estimated from radar.
The report was relayed through mPING. The event time is adjusted based on radar observations.
